comment: The sources that gate an unbuilt tool, and what the last probe found. A gate's reason is a claim about a URL on a date, and this is the dated part. scripts/probe-build-gates.mjs re-probes every row and prints what changed; test/unit/build-gates.test.js keeps the rows honest against docs/unbuilt-tools.md. Reachable does NOT mean buildable: a reachable row still needs the document read and the tool written.

gates.source: Fine, Eames and Heymann, "Herd immunity: a rough guide", Clin Infect Dis 2011;52:911
gates.note: PubMed record 21427399 carries no PMC id, so there is no open copy; the full texts that surface are a course-site PDF and a document-sharing upload, neither a publisher copy nor a verified reprint.

gates.source: Lwanga and Lemeshow, Sample Size Determination in Health Studies, WHO 1991 (ISBN 9241544058)
gates.note: The search page answers, the book is not in it. A priced 1991 WHO publication with no IRIS copy; the reachable PDFs are third-party scans on university and document-sharing servers, which are not verified reprints. A 200 here means the catalogue is up, not that the manual is available.

gates.source: OPTN, Guide to Calculating and Interpreting the KDPI
gates.note: Re-probed November 7, 2026. The HTML pages on www.hrsa.gov/optn now open in a browser (the KDPI calculator page, last reviewed December 2025, links the guide and the mapping table at hrsa.gov/sites/default/files/hrsa/optn/kdpi_guide.pdf and kdpi_mapping_table.pdf), but both PDFs arrive as file downloads, and a scripted fetch is refused. Getting past that refusal with a disguised client would defeat a bot check, so the two PDFs still need saving by hand.

gates.source: OPTN, Guide to Calculating and Interpreting the EPTS
gates.note: Half open. The guide (updated April 7, 2026; SHA-256 a62d935a…, saved by hand) was read November 7, 2026, and its formula reproduces all three worked examples to seven decimals (openspec design, tool 2). The score is a percentile from the EPTS mapping table, a separate PDF (hrsa.gov/sites/default/files/hrsa/optn/epts_mapping_table.pdf) that arrives as a download and is still to be saved by hand. Without it the tool could print only the raw value, not the 20% line allocation uses.

gates.source: CMS Hospital OQR Specifications Manual (OP-18, OP-22)
gates.note: A 200 that carries nothing: the page is a 5.7 KB single-page-application shell whose only hrefs are its own bundle, favicon and stylesheet. The manual is behind a client-side fetch, so a status code alone would read this gate as open. Re-probed November 7, 2026 in a browser: the page renders and lists the 2027 manual (version 20.0, ED-Throughput set 1d_ED_Throughput_set_v20.0.pdf) and the 2026 manual (19.0a). A script still gets the HTML shell, and opening a PDF first asks the reader to accept the AMA's CPT license. Accepting a license is the owner's decision, so the set is still unread.

gates.source: Westgard, Barry, Hunt and Groth, Clin Chem 1981;27:493 (for the three-level rules 2of3-2s, 3-1s, 6-x, 9-x)
gates.note: The classic two-level rules shipped in spec-v1691 from the first author's own published account; the three-level alternatives were gated on the paper specifically and stay unevaluated.
The abstract-level summary says "10% to 15% weekly dose changes" only, which is not an algorithm.

gates.source: AHA/ASA 2026 guideline for the early management of acute ischemic stroke, Stroke 2026
gates.note: Shipped in spec-v1708 (November 7, 2026). The guideline turned out to be Free Access in a browser (the 403 was to scripts); its recommendation tables and Table 8 are images, read at full resolution, and its July 27, 2026 correction was read. Kept as a record of the gate that held it from July to November 2026.

gates.source: Hull and Sarubbi, Ann Intern Med 1976;85:183
gates.note: The decisive problem is not only reach: two incompatible coefficient sets circulate (k = 0.00293 x CrCl + 0.014 against 0.0024 x CrCl + 0.01) and neither primary paper is open, so a dosing tool cannot pick one.

gates.source: Levey and Jennings, Am J Clin Pathol 1950;20:1059 (task 1.5, cited for the chart's name only)
gates.note: Also searched the Internet Archive, which this project has used for a 1922 paper: its AJCP 1950 holding is a volume index only, not the issues. The task's own fallback applies, and levey-jennings-limits says the paper was not opened.

gates.source: An FDA final rule on certain distributions of compounded human drug products, or an updated standard MOU
gates.note: There is no document to probe. The tool is built once one of them exists.

gates.source: A rebate model that survives challenge
gates.note: The earlier pilot was vacated in February 2026 and the revised model may be challenged again.

gates.source: Real patient-access API exports to test against
gates.note: Built after January 1, 2027, when the exports exist.
FDA's October 2025 enforcement notices conflict with the schedule's 6-months-to-3-years cell, so the tool is not wanted rather than not reachable.
